The Large Blue Horses

Franz Marc, 1911

Oil on canvas

Three blue horses against red and yellow hills, painted in bold, flat colour.

Use this style

Franz Marc, The Large Blue Horses, 1911. Walker Art Center, Minneapolis. Source on Wikimedia Commons. Licence: Public domain.

About the painting

Franz Marc painted The Large Blue Horses in 1911, the year he and Kandinsky founded the Blaue Reiter group in Munich. Marc gave colours meanings of their own: in a letter to August Macke he called blue the male principle, stern and spiritual. Three horses fill the canvas, their curved backs echoing the red and yellow hills behind them.

Marc painted animals because he felt they lived more purely than people. He was killed at Verdun in 1916, at 36. The painting has been in the Walker Art Center in Minneapolis since 1942.

How it looks on your photo

One of the most colourful styles. Photos turn deep blue and violet with red and yellow accents, and outlines become rounded, rhythmic curves. It is striking on animals and landscapes. At high intensity it overwhelms small detail.
